analysis.one_liner: Bajaj Finserv is a holding company that owns the controlling stakes in the Bajaj Group's financial businesses - lending (Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Housing Finance), life insurance and general insurance - so its earnings are really the sum of those subsidiaries' results.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 2026) results were declared on 3 Nov 2026, just days ago. Consolidated PAT attributable to shareholders came in around ₹2,758-2,760 crore (sources differ by a couple of crore), up about 23% year-on-year, on total income of ₹43,416 crore (up ~17%). The lending arm Bajaj Finance grew PAT 29% with improving loan quality, life insurance new-business margins expanded sharply, but the general insurance business saw profit fall on claims pressure.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of Bajaj Finserv as a basket holding pieces of four businesses: a large lending company, a housing finance company, and two insurance companies. When you buy the stock you are buying a slice of all four at once. The tension here is that the businesses inside the basket are growing earnings nicely - lending profit up 29%, life insurance new business margin up sharply - but the basket itself (the stock price) has gone almost nowhere for five years and has badly lagged both the broader market and its own sister holding company. Good news inside the businesses has not shown up in the share price.
analysis.quarters: H1 FY27 consolidated PAT was ₹12,249 crore, up 21.6% year-on-year, on total income of ₹85,453 crore (+17.8%). In the latest quarter (Q2 FY27), Bajaj Finance's consolidated PAT rose 29% to ₹6,367 crore as AUM grew 26% to ₹5.84 lakh crore and asset quality improved (gross NPA fell from 1.24% to 1.06%). Bajaj Life Insurance's value of new business rose 40% to ₹512 crore with new-business margin expanding from 17.1% to 21.6%, though its solvency ratio slipped from 346% to 255% year-on-year (still well above the 150% regulatory floor, but the direction is worth watching). Bajaj General Insurance's profit fell to ₹420 crore from ₹517 crore a year earlier despite premiums growing 10%, as claims pressure bit into margins - this is the one segment where growth did not translate into profit, and it should not be waved away as a one-off without checking the combined ratio, which was not available in the sources checked.
analysis.performance_read: The uncomfortable fact here is that the stock has delivered essentially nothing over five years (+0.3%) while the Nifty returned 36.6% and the group's own sister holding company, Bajaj Holdings, returned 134% over the same period - a wide and persistent underperformance despite the underlying businesses growing profits at double-digit rates. Over three years the pattern repeats: Bajaj Finserv +17% versus Nifty +27% and peer +60%. The stock trades about 43% below its all-time peak of ₹3,197, but that peak was recorded on 17 May 2006 - more than a year before Bajaj Auto's 2007-08 demerger created Bajaj Finserv as a separate listed entity. That peak figure reflects a stitched-together pre-demerger price series for the undivided Bajaj Auto group, not a genuine peak of today's Bajaj Finserv business, so the 42.7% 'drawdown' should not be read as a crash in this company - it is largely a data-continuity artifact. The 5:1 stock split of September 2022 is already reflected in the price series supplied and does not distort these return figures.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 30.5x trailing earnings and about 3.85x book value against an ROE near 15.4% (figures sourced from aggregators, not independently cross-checked against Screener - treat as approximate), the stock is not statistically cheap. Why it carries this multiple: as a holding company its value is really a sum of its parts - a premium-rated NBFC (Bajaj Finance), a fast-growing life insurer, a general insurer, and a newly listed housing finance arm - and the market has historically paid up for that basket. Whether it is actually cheap is a separate question: earnings have compounded at 20%+ for several years while the share price has stood still, meaning the multiple has quietly compressed - the market may be pricing in regulatory risk to the lending book, volatility in general insurance claims, or simply a preference for the sister holding company's structure over this one.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is real but mixed in quality across segments. The lending business (Bajaj Finance) is genuinely volume-led - AUM up 26%, 4.4 million new customers added in the quarter - and margin quality is improving alongside it, since NPAs are falling rather than being masked by growth. Life insurance growth is more margin-led: new business margin expanded from 17.1% to 21.6%, a healthier mix shift rather than just writing more low-margin policies. General insurance is the weak spot - premium grew but profit fell, meaning growth there is not translating into durable earnings and should not be counted as a growth driver until claims experience stabilises.
analysis.health_read: As a holding company, Bajaj Finserv's own cash flow depends on dividends and value accretion from its subsidiaries rather than its own operations. The signals from the largest subsidiary, Bajaj Finance, are reassuring on business risk - gross and net NPAs both fell year-on-year even as the loan book grew 26%, suggesting profit growth there is backed by improving credit quality, not deteriorating underwriting. The more pressing concern is regulatory and structural risk rather than balance-sheet distress: the RBI's August 2026 draft proposal to restrict revolving/flexi credit products could affect roughly 15% of Bajaj Finance's AUM, forcing a product shift to term loans from November 2026, and the life insurer's solvency ratio has declined substantially (346% to 255% year-on-year) even though it remains well-capitalised.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 58.65% of the company; no pledging was found in the sources checked, though that should be verified directly against the latest BSE shareholding disclosure rather than taken as confirmed zero. FIIs hold about 8.16% and DIIs about 11.1%. The most significant ownership change is structural rather than at the Bajaj Finserv level itself: Allianz SE, the German insurer that was a 24-year joint-venture partner holding roughly 26% of both the life and general insurance arms, fully exited by March 2026 after the Bajaj Group bought out its stake in two tranches (January and March 2026); the insurers were subsequently rebranded Bajaj Life Insurance and Bajaj General Insurance. No well-known individual investor was flagged as being on the register in the sources checked - if a name is expected here, say so, but none surfaced.
strengths: Bajaj Finance (largest subsidiary) grew consolidated PAT 29% YoY to ₹6,367 crore while gross NPA improved from 1.24% to 1.06%, showing growth paired with better asset quality, not worse
Bajaj Life Insurance's value of new business rose 40% YoY to ₹512 crore with new-business margin expanding from 17.1% to 21.6%
Consolidated H1 FY27 PAT grew 21.6% to ₹12,249 crore, continuing a multi-year streak of double-digit profit growth

Full buyout of Allianz SE's stake in both insurance arms (completed March 2026) gives the group complete economic ownership of two previously 74-76%-owned subsidiaries, removing a minority-interest drag on future profit attribution
watchpoints: The stock has returned just +0.3% over five years versus +36.6% for the Nifty and +134% for sister company Bajaj Holdings, despite strong subsidiary earnings growth - a persistent re-rating gap that has not closed

RBI's draft norms (August 2026) targeting revolving/flexi credit products could affect roughly 15% of Bajaj Finance's loan book; the transition to replacement term-loan products began only from 1 November 2026 and its impact on growth and margins is untested
Bajaj General Insurance's profit fell to ₹420 crore from ₹517 crore YoY despite 10% premium growth, indicating claims pressure that has not yet been resolved
Bajaj Life Insurance's solvency ratio fell from 346% to 255% year-on-year - still comfortably above the 150% regulatory minimum, but the pace of decline is worth monitoring over the next few quarters
analysis.one_thing: Watch how Bajaj Finance's new term-loan products (replacing flexi/revolving credit from 1 November 2026 under RBI's draft norms) perform on growth and margins over the next two quarters, and whether that - combined with any recovery in general insurance claims experience - is enough to close the five-year gap between subsidiary earnings growth and the stock's flat long-term return.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 PAT figure was cross-checked across three sources (apacnewsnetwork, sahi.com, angelone.in) and is consistent to within roughly ₹2 crore - treated as reliable. Valuation ratios (P/E ~30.5x, P/B ~3.85x, ROE ~15.4%) came from aggregator sites (univest.in, valueresearchonline.com) and were not independently verified against Screener or the company's own filing - check there before relying on them. Promoter pledging could not be confirmed either way from sources checked and should be verified on the latest BSE shareholding disclosure. The -42.7% drawdown-from-peak figure supplied is based on a 17 May 2006 peak that predates Bajaj Finserv's 2007-08 demerger from Bajaj Auto; this reflects a stitched pre-demerger price series, not a genuine peak/crash of the current business, and should be read with that caveat. The next scheduled results date (Q3 FY27) has not yet been announced.
